output.title: Positioning drift usually starts in the workflow, not the logo
output.body:
Positioning drift usually starts in the workflow, not the logo.

For a small business, drift shows up when what you say in one place no longer matches what you actually deliver or charge. Your website says one thing, your proposal says another, and your invoice or email signature quietly tells a third story. That is not a brand mystery. It is a workflow problem.

The practical next step is simple: audit your last five proposals, invoices, or customer conversations against your current website and email wording. Look for one clear mismatch. Maybe the site still promises a support level you no longer offer. Maybe the proposal template says one scope, but your delivery has moved on. Maybe the price language is out of date.

Then make one owner decision: update the wording, or change the delivery so it matches the promise. Keep that decision human. If money or scope is changing, the business owner should approve it.

If you later automate parts of the workflow, fix the positioning first. Otherwise the system just repeats the mismatch faster. A tidy workflow is less dramatic than a new logo, but it tends to be more useful.
